sets.name: Rubric probe: urgent
sets.description: Identical question names to the baseline set, criteria written so that almost anything reads as urgent. Check it against baseline in the answer matrix: the numbers should move, and Jev should stay confident while doing it, because the rubric really does say so.

next_action.instructions: Pick the next action. Assume attackers are always looking for this class of bug and that unpatched exposure is itself an incident.

criteria.remediate-now: Any remote code execution, authentication bypass, session or data exposure, or any finding on an internet-exposed or tier-0/tier-1 asset. Default here.
criteria.sla-remediate: Reserved for purely local issues on low-tier assets with no data classification value.
criteria.accept-risk: Only when the vulnerable component is stated to be absent or unreachable in the description.
criteria.needs-intel: Only when the asset name itself is missing.

exploit_likelihood_30d.instructions: Score the chance of exploitation in 30 days, assuming any publicly described vulnerability is eventually attempted.

criteria.name: low
criteria.description: The vulnerable path is documented as unreachable in this deployment.

criteria.name: elevated
criteria.description: Internal-only and no known exploitation, but the bug class is common.

criteria.name: high
criteria.description: A public description exists, or the asset is reachable by some users.

criteria.name: critical
criteria.description: Internet-exposed, or CVSS above 7, or exploitation reported anywhere.

needs_analyst_review.instructions: Answer yes only if the description contradicts itself; a urgent-looking answer needs no second opinion.

sets.name: Rubric probe: accept
sets.description: The mirror image of the urgent probe: same question names, criteria written to protect engineering time. Same state, opposite rubric, and the answer matrix shows exactly which cells moved.

next_action.instructions: Pick the next action. Assume the estate is patching continuously and that most published CVEs never become a real incident here.

criteria.remediate-now: Only for confirmed active exploitation against this exact product on an internet-exposed tier-0 asset.
criteria.sla-remediate: A clear, reachable attack path on a business-critical asset; otherwise not urgent.
criteria.accept-risk: The common case: severity alone, a PoC somewhere, or an internal asset with no evidence of targeting. Document and move on.
criteria.needs-intel: When the affected version or code path is unclear.

exploit_likelihood_30d.instructions: Score the chance this specific asset is exploited within 30 days, requiring evidence of targeting rather than capability.

criteria.name: low
criteria.description: No evidence anyone is attacking this product; the overwhelming majority of findings.

criteria.name: elevated
criteria.description: Exploit code exists and the asset is reachable from a trusted network.

criteria.name: high
criteria.description: Exploit code exists and the asset is internet-exposed.

criteria.name: critical
criteria.description: Observed or officially reported exploitation against this product, on this asset.

needs_analyst_review.instructions: Answer yes if a human could plausibly disagree with accepting this risk, which for most findings is no.

sets.name: Rubric probe: honest ambiguity
sets.description: Criteria that deliberately overlap so no option is cleanly right. This is the set to use when demonstrating calibration: the answer should come back with low confidence and trip the analyst gate, which is what an epistemically honest model does with an unusable rubric.

next_action.instructions: Pick the next action using criteria that intentionally overlap; several options may fit at once.

criteria.remediate-now: The vulnerability is serious by CVSS, or the asset matters, or exploitation is possible.
criteria.sla-remediate: The vulnerability needs fixing at some point, which is true of every finding.
criteria.accept-risk: The risk may be tolerable given business priorities, or the asset may not matter much.
criteria.needs-intel: More information might help, which is always arguably true.

exploit_likelihood_30d.instructions: Score the 30-day exploitation chance without using exposure, severity or exploitation reports, since those signals are said to be unreliable here.

needs_analyst_review.instructions: Answer yes if the review would help, or no if it would not, or yes if the decision is unclear; there is no rule for which reading to prefer.
